Multiplicity three forces a length-four arithmetic progression. If no class has multiplicity three, a (2,2,2) profile would force after normalization A={0,1,2,t}; the only nondegenerate candidates t=4 or -2 require [4]=[3], which forces p=7, so p≥11 leaves exactly four profiles. Singleton classes contribute fixed 2 per class, while explicit unimodular sign choices cancel the doubled autocorrelations in the non-AP profiles, giving 28,24,20. For an AP, writing adjacent phase ratios and r=|1+z| reduces the variable part to (r-1)^2+r^2≥1/2, yielding 19; the displayed exact phases attain equality. The verifier exhausts profiles for seven primes and checks constructions; an independent profile replay for small p≥11 reproduced the four-profile classification.
